# CLI reference

Generated from the command tree of `holaclaw`, grouped as `holaclaw help`
groups it.

- Long flags take two dashes: `--config`. The single-dash spelling (`-config`)
  is not accepted. One-letter shorthands take one: `-m`, `-q`, `-h`, and
  `-v`, which counts: `-vv` is two.
- Flags may come before or after the arguments, except in `auth set`,
  `memory add` and `memory search`: there everything after the first argument is
  taken as typed, so a value or a text may start with a dash. `--` ends the flags
  anywhere.
- `-h`, `--help` and `holaclaw help <command>` print help to stdout and exit 0. A
  wrong invocation — an unknown command or flag, a missing argument — prints the
  error and the usage to stderr and exits 2; any other failure exits 1.
- The config directory is `--config`, else `$HOLACLAW_CONFIG`, else `/etc/holaclaw`. When
  `/etc/holaclaw` does not exist, a user other than root gets `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/holaclaw`
  (`~/.config/holaclaw`) instead, and the control socket `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/holaclaw.sock`.
  Commands that talk to the daemon take `--addr` and `--token`, else
  `$HOLACLAW_ADDR` and `$HOLACLAW_TOKEN`, else the socket of the config directory.
- `holaclaw completion bash|zsh|fish|powershell` prints a shell completion script.

## Global flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--config string` |  | config directory |

### `holaclaw init`

write a config for one provider, and create the owner

```
usage: holaclaw init [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--base-url string` |  | the endpoint of --provider openai-compat, e.g. http://localhost:11434/v1 |
| `--model string` |  | the model id, instead of the provider's default |
| `--non-interactive` |  | never prompt, even at a terminal (without one on stdin init never prompts) |
| `--provider string` |  | the provider to write a config for: openai\|openai-codex\|openrouter\|openai-compat |
| `--token-file string` |  | also create an init binding with one admin token, and write the token to this new file, mode 0600 |

## chat

### `holaclaw chat`

talk to an agent in the terminal

```
usage: holaclaw chat [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--addr string` |  | daemon base URL or socket path ($HOLACLAW_ADDR) |
| `--agent string` | `main` | agent name |
| `-c`, `--continue` |  | resume the most recent conversation instead of starting a new one |
| `-m`, `--message string` |  | send one message and exit |
| `--plain` |  | line-by-line output instead of the full-screen UI |
| `-q`, `--quiet` |  | no progress lines while a turn runs |
| `-r`, `--resume string` |  | resume this conversation instead of starting a new one; without one, choose from the most recent |
| `--token string` |  | API token, for a TCP address; prefer $HOLACLAW_TOKEN — an argument is visible to every process in "ps" |
| `--trace` |  | print the trace id after each reply |
| `-v`, `--verbose` |  | -v also shows tool calls and results, -vv tool arguments and browser moves, -vvv full tool responses (--plain only; the UI has a details panel) |

### `holaclaw auth`

manage the secrets in auth.toml

```
usage: holaclaw auth
```

#### `holaclaw auth set`

store one secret

```
usage: holaclaw auth set <providers|channels>.<name> <key> [value] [flags]

with no value the secret is read from stdin: printf %s "$KEY" | holaclaw auth set providers.openrouter api_key
a multi-line secret (a service-account key) is read whole from stdin: holaclaw auth set channels.googlechat service_account < key.json
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-verify` |  | store a channel bot token or service-account key without checking it with the platform |


### `holaclaw completion`

print a shell completion script (bash | zsh | fish | powershell)

```
usage: holaclaw completion

Generate the autocompletion script for holaclaw for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.
```

#### `holaclaw completion bash`

Generate the autocompletion script for bash

```
usage: holaclaw completion bash

Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(holaclaw completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	holaclaw completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/holaclaw

#### macOS:

	holaclaw completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/holaclaw

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` |  | disable completion descriptions |

#### `holaclaw completion zsh`

Generate the autocompletion script for zsh

```
usage: holaclaw completion zsh [flags]

Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(holaclaw completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	holaclaw completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_holaclaw"

#### macOS:

	holaclaw completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_holaclaw

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` |  | disable completion descriptions |

Generate the autocompletion script for fish

```
usage: holaclaw completion fish [flags]

Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	holaclaw completion fish | source

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

	holaclaw completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/holaclaw.fish

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` |  | disable completion descriptions |

Generate the autocompletion script for powershell

### `holaclaw connectors`

connect remote MCP servers to holaclaw

```
usage: holaclaw connectors
```

#### `holaclaw connectors create`

connect a remote MCP server

```
usage: holaclaw connectors create <id> <url> [flags]

a server that needs a sign-in answers with an authorization URL. By default the command prints it
and returns: open it in any browser, sign in, and pass the address the browser lands on to
`holaclaw connectors code`. With --listen the command receives that redirect itself on 127.0.0.1,
ports 26500 to 26504, and waits until the connector is connected
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--addr string` |  | daemon base URL or socket path ($HOLACLAW_ADDR) |
| `--allow-insecure-transport` |  | reach the server over plain http on any host, or https with a certificate that does not verify |
| `--auth string` |  | none or oauth; what discovery finds when omitted |
| `--client-id string` |  | a client id registered with the authorization server |
| `--client-secret-stdin` |  | read the secret of the pre-registered client from stdin |
| `--listen` |  | receive the redirect on 127.0.0.1 and wait until connected |
| `--scopes stringSlice` | `[]` | scopes to ask for, comma separated; every scope the server offers when omitted |
| `--token string` |  | API token, for a TCP address; prefer $HOLACLAW_TOKEN — an argument is visible to every process in "ps" |

#### `holaclaw connectors reconnect`

sign in to a connector again, optionally with other scopes

```
usage: holaclaw connectors reconnect <id> [flags]

the old sign-in serves until the new one is done. The modes are those of create
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--addr string` |  | daemon base URL or socket path ($HOLACLAW_ADDR) |
| `--client-secret-stdin` |  | read the secret of the pre-registered client from stdin |
| `--listen` |  | receive the redirect on 127.0.0.1 and wait until connected |
| `--scopes stringSlice` | `[]` | scopes to ask for, comma separated; the connector's scopes when omitted |
| `--token string` |  | API token, for a TCP address; prefer $HOLACLAW_TOKEN — an argument is visible to every process in "ps" |

#### `holaclaw invite create`

create a one-shot expiring invite code for an identity or a room

```
usage: holaclaw invite create [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--addr string` |  | daemon base URL or socket path ($HOLACLAW_ADDR) |
| `--channel string` |  | the one channel instance the code redeems on; holaclaw pairs a device |
| `--identity string` |  | identity id (from "holaclaw identity list") the redeemed account is bound to; it gets that identity's role |
| `--room` |  | approve a room instead of binding a person; telegram, googlechat and whatsapp only: telegram's link adds the bot to a group (a room), Chat has no deep link, so send "@app \<code>" in the space |
| `--scope string` |  | holaclaw only: token scope of the paired device, client \| admin (default client) |
| `--token string` |  | API token, for a TCP address; prefer $HOLACLAW_TOKEN — an argument is visible to every process in "ps" |
| `--ttl duration` |  | how long the code stays valid (default 15m, at most 1h, or 24h for an identity with no bindings) |

| `--token string` |  | API token, for a TCP address; prefer $HOLACLAW_TOKEN — an argument is visible to every process in "ps" |

### `holaclaw token`

manage the API tokens

```
usage: holaclaw token
```

#### `holaclaw token create`

create an API token; the secret is shown once

```
usage: holaclaw token create (--identity <id> | --binding holaclaw:<alias>) --name <name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--addr string` |  | daemon base URL or socket path ($HOLACLAW_ADDR) |
| `--binding string` |  | existing holaclaw:\<alias> binding to add the token to |
| `--identity string` |  | identity the token acts as, through a new holaclaw binding |
| `--name string` |  | token name, also the name of a new binding |
| `--scope string` |  | client \| admin (default client); admin needs the role owner or admin |
| `--token string` |  | API token, for a TCP address; prefer $HOLACLAW_TOKEN — an argument is visible to every process in "ps" |

#### `holaclaw token list`

list the active API tokens

```
usage: holaclaw token list [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--addr string` |  | daemon base URL or socket path ($HOLACLAW_ADDR) |
| `--all` |  | include revoked tokens |
| `--binding string` |  | only the tokens of this holaclaw:\<alias> binding |
| `--identity string` |  | only the tokens of this identity |
| `--token string` |  | API token, for a TCP address; prefer $HOLACLAW_TOKEN — an argument is visible to every process in "ps" |

#### `holaclaw token set`

raise or lower a token's scope

```
usage: holaclaw token set <id> --scope client|admin [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--addr string` |  | daemon base URL or socket path ($HOLACLAW_ADDR) |
| `--scope string` |  | client \| admin; admin needs the role owner or admin |
| `--token string` |  | API token, for a TCP address; prefer $HOLACLAW_TOKEN — an argument is visible to every process in "ps" |

#### `holaclaw token rotate`

replace a token with a new secret on the same binding; the old one is revoked

```
usage: holaclaw token rotate <id> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--addr string` |  | daemon base URL or socket path ($HOLACLAW_ADDR) |
| `--token string` |  | API token, for a TCP address; prefer $HOLACLAW_TOKEN — an argument is visible to every process in "ps" |

#### `holaclaw token revoke`

revoke an API token; its binding stays

```
usage: holaclaw token revoke <id> [flags]
```

|---|---|---|
